restrictions: Applies to the selected target poseidon-orchard-r8-prefix-v1 only (eight partial rounds 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 plus the eight fixed full rounds); the construction uses the first two full rounds being skippable on a line and gives no claim for other round counts.

time_log2 is the operation count of the algorithm (at most two centres, K = 2, isolation at its 64-round cap, one thread) plus the 1,000,000-op offline bound, declared preprocessing_log2 = 20, inside time_log2. Two changes on our filed r = 8 entry e9be6981: (i) K = 2 centres, stage D the lean cofactor-free half-gcd charged for the normal remainder sequence with the quotient and return tests and the ABORT on any other case (bradcush e6dcb600/1aa56884, gta6rp bef31fdd, proof.md 4.4, 6.3, 9.5), row 186,607,764,971,971; H-NORMAL enters only the success probability and an abnormal trial ABORTs after a prefix of the work, so the time bound holds for every sequence; (ii) stage C in the value domain, 364 cosets of size h = 2^23, VSHIFT = 2 (bradcush 4bcabff8, proof.md 4.3V), row 445,002,702,221,819. N_max = 1,270,543,047,015,334. Cost model orchard-field-ram-v2: each field op, load, store, control op and random word priced 1/C, C = 216 + 21 r = 384.

memory_log2_bytes = 39.010 is the footprint: the arena is the capacity of the two-ended allocator of proof.md 4.2 on the allocation/free sequence of one trial (the trials run one after the other from the same allocator state), its high-water mark reached in stage D holding the normal-case division arrays (an abnormal trial ABORTs after a prefix of these allocations), two-ended pool 553,459,655,424 + 128 bytes, slab classes 46,377,216 bytes and stages E and later 16,896 bytes = 553,506,049,664 bytes, plus 5,250,444 bytes of code and static data and a 65,536-byte stack, 553,511,365,644 bytes = 2^39.010, rounded up at three decimals (proof.md 7; the allocation/free sequence and its arena high-water mark are reproduced event by event in Appendix E). No stored advice; the twiddle table is built at run time and charged in stage init.

success_probability 0.615723989999992894 is a probability over the algorithm's fresh independent uniform 256-bit random words (the cost model's random-word primitive) for the fixed target, derived from the premises H-ONE and H-NORMAL as 1 - (1 - q + delta)^K - K (eps_coin + eps_iso) with K = 2, q = 0.3901 (H-ONE), delta = 0.01 (H-NORMAL, proof.md 9.5), eps_iso < 2^-48, eps_coin < 2^-128 (proof.md 9.1, 9.2, 9.5). The value the formula gives with the stated eps bounds is 0.615723989999992894 (>= the organizer floor 0.39). Stage D is charged for the normal remainder sequence with the ABORT (proof.md 6.3); H-NORMAL enters only this bound, not the time or memory. The value-domain stage C reproduces R = S^((p-1)/2) mod g exactly (proved in proof.md 4.3V in closed form from coset distinctness, h | p - 1 and 2 n1 >= 2m + 1, no premise), so H-ONE and its bound are unchanged.

heuristics.statement: Notation: p is the Pallas prime, D = 5^14, F in F_p[X] the fixed digest polynomial of proof.md section 2.3 at r = 8 (degree D), g_c the monic odd part of F about the centre c (proof.md section 3, degree m = 3,051,757,812), k(c) the number of nonzero squares S with g_c(S) = 0 (k(c) = deg G of stage D). Premise: the number of centres c in F_p with 1 <= k(c) <= 16 is at least 0.3901 p, i.e. P(E_c) >= q = 0.3901 for c uniform on F_p. With K = 2 and the premise H-NORMAL (delta = 0.01) the success bound is 1 - (1 - q + delta)^2 - 2 (eps_coin + eps_iso) = 0.615723989999992894 (proof.md 9.2). The value-domain stage C and the ABORT cofactor-free stage D of this entry change only how R = S^((p-1)/2) mod g is computed and how the gcd is driven, not R or the gcd degree, so H-ONE, its role, scope, extrapolation, evidence and limitations are identical to our filed r = 8 entry e9be6981.
heuristics.scope: The fixed Poseidon target poseidon-orchard-r8-prefix-v1, this line construction, centres uniform on F_p. Not claimed for other round counts. The value-domain stage C and the cofactor-free in-place stage D are program changes under the declared cost model; H-ONE bounds the fraction of good centres. The success bound also uses H-NORMAL (delta = 0.01, proof.md 9.5), which enters only the success probability: stage D is charged for the normal remainder sequence with the ABORT (proof.md 6.3), so the time and memory hold for every sequence.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the law of k(c) at reduced depth to the polynomial F of depth 14. The roots of G(c,t) = g_c(t^2) in t are +-t_1, ..., +-t_m, so the monodromy group of the cover lies in the hyperoctahedral group B_m and k(c) counts the positive fixed points of the Frobenius element; for the full group B_m this number is Poisson(1/2) in the limit, P(k >= 1) = 1 - e^(-1/2) = 0.3934693 (exactly 1 - sum_{j<=m} (-1/2)^j/j!), and Bonferroni at order 4 gives P >= 151/384 = 0.3932292 from four moments (proof.md 9.3(a), (b)). At N = 2 and 3 S-box layers on the deployed constants and the line of this construction the arithmetic monodromy is B_12 and B_62 (Grok jobs 136 and 137, re-run on the deployed constants, proof.md 10.3); the geometric monodromy then contains the commutator subgroup of B_m, the j-fold fibre powers are absolutely irreducible, and the Aubry-Perret bound with Bonferroni gives 0.39346933 <= P(1 <= k <= 16) <= 0.39346944 there: the premise is a theorem at those depths (proof.md 9.3(c)). Measured: toy fields at p = 1,048,627, exact over all centres, 27 cases with 3 to 8 layers, P(k >= 1) between 0.39214 and 0.39436 (proof.md 9.3(d)); the organizer-run tests euclid-normal-n2-t256-l2-a and euclid-normal-n3-t24 compute the algorithm's own pairs at depth N = 2, 3 (m = 12, 62) per organizer seed and report the gcd-positive count, positive in about two of five trials (E[k] about 1/2, Binomial fraction 0.393469), corroborating H-ONE (proof.md 10.5.1). The deviations from the law shrink like p^(-1/2) and do not grow with the degree (toy fields 1.36/sqrt(p); the counts of Grok job 139, eps ~ 3.1/sqrt(p) over degrees 5 to 1,953,125); the premise extrapolates the law to N = 14 with an allowance stated exactly as 0.0033693.
heuristics.limitations: It concerns this F, not every polynomial of degree D: it is false for permutation polynomials (k = 0 at every centre) and for a decomposable F with imprimitive monodromy, and false at one layer (m = 2: the law gives exactly 0.375). At N = 14 the monodromy is not computed and the counts N_3, N_4 are out of reach of Weil's bound; the premise is the extrapolation of a law that is a theorem at N = 2, 3 and measured on toy fields and on the real field at N <= 4. The value-domain stage C adds no premise: coset distinctness is a closed-form certificate (proof.md 4.3V), and the equality of the value-domain and coefficient-domain R is proved in 4.3V in closed form (no premise); the ABORT cofactor-free in-place stage D computes the same remainder sequence and the same gcd and is charged for the normal sequence (proof.md 6.3); H-NORMAL enters only the success bound (proof.md 9.5), not the cost or memory.

heuristics.statement: For the centre c uniform on F_p, the Euclidean remainder sequence of (g_c, R_c - 1), where g_c is the monic odd part of proof.md section 3 (degree m = 3,051,757,812) and R_c = S^((p-1)/2) mod g_c, is normal down to its gcd (deg(R_c - 1) = m - 1 and every quotient has degree 1) except with probability at most delta = 0.01 (2^-6.64). Stage D is charged for the normal sequence; every division tests its quotient degree and every call of the half-gcd its return, and on any other case the trial ends (ABORT, proof.md 4.4, 6.3). With H-ONE the success bound is 1 - (1 - q + delta)^2 - 2 (eps_coin + eps_iso) = 0.615723989999992894 with q = 0.3901 and K = 2 (proof.md 9.2).
heuristics.scope: The pairs (g_c, R_c - 1) of the target poseidon-orchard-r8-prefix-v1, c uniform on F_p. It enters only the success probability: the time and memory bounds hold for every remainder sequence, because a trial with an abnormal sequence ends at its first failed test after executing a prefix of the charged work (proof.md 6.3). Not claimed for other round counts. The premise is bradcush's (entries e6dcb600 and 1aa56884); the allowance delta = 0.01 and the organizer-run tests follow gta6rp's entries (bef31fdd).
heuristics.extrapolation: For a uniformly random pair of degrees m and m - 1 the sequence is abnormal exactly when one of the m principal subresultant coefficients vanishes, each a nonzero polynomial of degree at most 2m in the coefficients, so by Schwartz-Zippel the probability is at most 2 m^2 / p < 2^-189; the premise extrapolates a much weaker form of this random-pair behaviour (delta = 0.01) to the structured pair (g_c, R_c - 1). Measured support, organizer-run (proof.md 10.5.1): the experiments euclid-normal-n2-t256-l2-a, euclid-normal-n3-t24 and euclid-normal-n4-t2 compute the complete Euclidean sequence of (g_c, R_c - 1) for this construction on the truncations F_2, F_3, F_4 (proof.md 10.3; m = 12, 62, 312), the first for 256 organizer-seeded trials of two centres each (512 sequences at m = 12), the others for 24 and 2 organizer-seeded centres, and return a witness pair exactly when the sequences are normal; the prediction is that every computed sequence is normal. Zero abnormal in the 512 sequences bounds the abnormality at m = 12 by 3/512 < delta = 0.01 (rule of three, one-sided 95%). Our runs of the same program: 1,066 sequences at m = 12, 62, 312, every quotient of degree 1.
heuristics.limitations: Not verified at r = 8, which would need the computation itself. The Schwartz-Zippel bound does not transfer, because the coefficients of R_c have degree about p in those of g_c; an algebraic relation between g_c and R_c that forces a principal subresultant coefficient to vanish for many centres would invalidate the premise, and none is known. The success bound stays at least 0.39 for every delta <= 0.1711 (proof.md 9.2), above the stated delta = 0.01. The organizer-run tests are at m = 12 to 312, far below m: they test the construction, not its scale; normality is computed inside the submitted program and the runner checks only the returned witness pairs.
